audit_findings.title: The perimeter contract is contaminated and misidentifies the Walker project
audit_findings.magnitude: $460.5m industrial-revenue-bond authorization subject to construction drawdowns; $1.92 per diluted share if treated as a direct cost, though it finances an operating asset
audit_findings.mechanism: Corrects the forecast perimeter and could alter growth, capital-spending classifications, owner earnings and available cash
audit_findings.evidence: On November 7, 2025, the Company closed an industrial revenue bond transaction with the Walker County Development Authority (the “Authority”) in order to receive a ten-year property tax incentive on the Company’s production facility in Walker County currently under development.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter description is demonstrably wrong: Walker's Deli and Hermitage AI are unrelated to the filed Walker County project. The valuation uses the as-filed business and no acquisition run-rate, so the metadata error alone does not invalidate the historical anchor. The facility's future spending, tax benefits and operating contribution could lower or raise value, but the record does not quantify their net effect or establish whether they change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Replace the perimeter contract with the PPC-filed Walker County development, obtain its construction schedule, sustaining-versus-growth capex classification, tax incentive and operating forecast, and rerun affected cash and growth assumptions.

audit_findings.title: Required capital spending and distributable cash may be inconsistently treated
audit_findings.magnitude: 2026 planned capex $900m-$950m; $490.4m incurred and $465.2m paid in the first six months; $388.843m cash added to equity; maintenance component unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially overstates recurring OE by understating maintenance capex and overstates the equity bridge by adding cash committed to operations or projects
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to fund these capital expenditures with cash flow from operations and cash on hand.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the capital program exceeds the entire cash balance added to value, although it does not identify how much is sustaining or non-distributable. The $388.843m cash addition equals $1.62 per share. Under the base DCF's computed sensitivity, a recurring OE overstatement of about $85.5m would erase the $3.50 price-to-buy-below cushion; if all added cash is unavailable, about $57.8m of recurring OE overstatement would do so. Those thresholds are small relative to the filed capital program, making this reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 and 2026 capex project by project into maintenance, efficiency and growth categories; establish minimum operating and committed-project cash; then rerun OE, the cash bridge and all scenarios without changing other assumptions.

audit_findings.title: The Mexican tax claim has material exposure above the recorded accrual
audit_findings.magnitude: $269.5m latest filed claim less $88.2m accrual = $181.3m unaccrued maximum; $0.75 per share before MOS and $0.53 per share after the 30% MOS
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse amount above the accrual would be deducted from equity or reduce future OE when paid
audit_findings.evidence: The amount under appeal for the remaining assessment, including any penalties and interest, is approximately $ 230.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The exposure is demonstrated, but the latest filing raises the appealed amount from $230.0m to $269.5m while retaining the $88.2m accrual. A full direct deduction of the $181.3m unaccrued balance is about 1.6% of the $11.663bn base equity value and would reduce the buy-below figure by approximately $0.53 per share, versus its $3.50 premium over the market price. On the filed maximum, this finding alone would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the $88.2m accrual remains embedded in historical OE, monitor the appeal and USMCA proceeding, and rerun the bridge only if probable exposure exceeds the filed $269.5m claim or recoveries change.

audit_findings.title: Open broiler antitrust claims could exceed recognized settlements
audit_findings.magnitude: Remaining additional loss unquantified; $93.906m litigation-settlement accrual at June 28, 2026; $838.5m incurred to date, including $155.4m in the first six months of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Unaccrued settlements would reduce equity or future OE; accrued but unpaid settlements also constrain cash added in the bridge
audit_findings.evidence: PPC continues to defend itself against the direct-action plaintiffs as well as parties that have opted out of the class settlements (collectively, the “Broiler Opt Outs”).
audit_findings.explanation: Open opt-out and Phase 2 claims are demonstrated, and the repeated filed charges show meaningful exposure. Historical expenses retained in OE cannot be deducted again, however, and the $838.5m incurred to date is not a measure of remaining loss. With no disclosed maximum or plaintiff-level reconciliation, the record cannot establish whether additional exposure can overcome the valuation cushion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $93.906m accrual to executed but unpaid settlements, identify remaining plaintiffs and claims, develop a supportable additional-loss range, and rerun the cash bridge or OE only for amounts not already recognized.

audit_findings.title: Potential asset-retirement obligations are absent from the balance sheet
audit_findings.mechanism: Facility renovation, closure or redevelopment could create cleanup capex, operating costs or a liability deducted from equity
audit_findings.evidence: Therefore, the Company has not recorded the fair value of any potential liability.
audit_findings.explanation: The absence of a recorded liability is demonstrated, but the filing states that settlement timing is indeterminate and that no renovation presently requires removal or remediation. The supplied record provides no site-level cost or triggering plan, so this is a forward-looking contingency rather than a presently measurable valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Monitor Walker construction, environmental upgrades and facility closures for triggering work; obtain site-level remediation estimates and rerun OE or the bridge when settlement becomes foreseeable and estimable.

audit_findings.title: A possible October 2026 coupon step-up is absent from historical owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 25-basis-point step-up on approximately $796.1m principal = about $1.99m annual pre-tax interest, 0.25% of $802.4m anchor OE and less than $10m undiscounted through 2031 maturity
audit_findings.mechanism: If triggered, the higher interest expense reduces forecast equity-level OE from October 15, 2026
audit_findings.evidence: From and including October 15, 2026, the interest rate payable on the notes shall be increased to 4.50 % per annum unless the Company has notified the trustee at least 30 days prior to October 15, 2026 that in respect of the year ended December 31, 2025, (1) the Company’s greenhouse gas emissions intensity reduction target of 17.679 % by December 31, 2025 from a 2019 baseline (the “Sustainability Performance Target”) has been satisfied and (2) the satisfaction of the Sustainability Performance Target has been confirmed by a qualified provider of third-party assurance or attestation services appointed by the Company to review the Company’s statement of the greenhouse gas emissions intensity in accordance with its customary procedures.
audit_findings.explanation: Historical OE correctly excludes a coupon change that had not begun. If the condition fails, the prospective annual reduction is approximately $0.008 per diluted share and less than $0.042 per share even before discounting the remaining cumulative payments. This is far below the $3.50 price-to-buy-below gap and cannot reasonably change the conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Confirm delivery of the required third-party emissions assurance; if absent, update forecast interest expense to 4.50% from October 15, 2026 while retaining the existing debt treatment.
